seam_notes: pof-mcp already had opt-in group gating keyed on POF_MCP_TOOL_GROUPS but nothing session-scoped: every session got all 50 tools regardless of who connected. Topology now resolves from the MCP initialize handshake's clientInfo (explicit clientInfo.topology first, then a name table), with the env path (POF_MCP_TOPOLOGY, then the HARNESS_MODE/CI shape e2e/helpers/ci-harness.ts uses) kept only as a fallback when the session declares nothing, and 'unknown' when neither speaks — unknown advertises the FULL surface, so an absent marker is never rendered as 'no editor'. Measured with the env vars blank: editor 50 tools, headless 46, web 46, nothing-declared 50 (was 50 for all four). The four withheld are the pof-bridge tools that need a live editor; pof_ue_status stays because it is the reachability probe and reports connected:false honestly. The editor-only list is guarded by a test asserting each named tool's own description says it needs a live editor — that guard failed on first run and exposed a real gap: pof_ue_test_results reads through pof-bridge but never said so; its description was corrected rather than the guard weakened.
falsifier: Set clientInfo.topology to 'editor' with POF_MCP_TOPOLOGY, HARNESS_MODE and CI all unset: if pof_ue_compile is absent from tools/list, the env read is back. Conversely a declared headless session that still lists it means the topology filter was dropped from advertisedTools. The direction is void if every client that reaches pof-mcp is spawned by PoF itself and always carries the marker — untrue today, since the Claude Code CLI connects over stdio from an .mcp.json entry that sets neither.
